# Your mission

Using everything from Modules 1–4, turn this skeleton into a polished
two-page briefing on the built-in `airquality` dataset (daily air quality
measurements in New York, May–September 1973). A finished example is in
`solutions/capstone-solution.qmd` — but build yours first.

# Requirements checklist

Your rendered PDF must include:

1. **Document setup** (Module 1)
   - [ ] A table of contents and numbered sections
   - [ ] A body font of your choice and 10pt base size

2. **Typst styling** (Module 2)
   - [ ] A `#show` rule that colours all level-1 headings
   - [ ] A key-findings box built with `#block` (fill + border + inset)
   - [ ] One statistic computed in R and typeset via the `output: asis`
         pattern (e.g. the maximum ozone reading and its date)

3. **Tables & figures** (Module 3)
   - [ ] A cross-referenced summary table (`tbl-` label) of monthly mean
         `Ozone`, `Temp` and `Wind`
   - [ ] A cross-referenced figure (`fig-` label) showing ozone vs
         temperature with a smoother
   - [ ] Two plots side by side using `layout-ncol`

4. **Stretch goal** (Module 4)
   - [ ] Render the whole thing through the `templates/` partials instead
         of inline styling (adjust the relative path:
         `../templates/typst-template.typ`)

# Data starter

```{r}
#| label: starter
#| echo: true
aq <- na.omit(airquality)
aq$MonthName <- month.name[aq$Month]
head(aq, 3)
```

Good luck — and remember `keep-typ: true` is your debugger.
